findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the assemble/route_criteria step as a second consumer of the --size-lines signal (thread it to plan_review_assemble_criteria's ctx.inputs so route_criteria's BUG_TIER_CRITERIA restriction is lifted on escalation), not just the precheck's ctx.inputs.
evidence: route_criteria (orchestrator.py:190-221) keys the bug tier off ctx.state (pctx from assemble_context) and restricts to registry.BUG_TIER_CRITERIA at :221 — a SEPARATE enforcement point from the precheck det_blocking=[] at workflow_ops.py:122

plan_review_assemble_criteria (workflow_ops.py:184-231) reads ctx.inputs.get('probe_criteria') at :226 — it consumes step inputs, but the gate YAML 'assemble' step (plan-review.yaml:49-53) only binds ticket_id + probe_criteria
--size-lines is a transient CLI flag (not a persisted state/file_impact field), so ctx.state.get('file_impact') at route_criteria:202 will not carry it
findings.finding: The --size-lines flag-threading enumeration in Scope names only 'the precheck's ctx.inputs read', but bug-tier escalation is enforced in TWO workflow steps — plan_review_precheck (workflow_ops.py:115, which forces det_blocking=[]) AND plan_review_assemble_criteria -> orchestrator.route_criteria (:221, which restricts the criteria set to BUG_TIER_CRITERIA). route_criteria reads pctx.state via assemble_context, and --size-lines is a transient CLI flag that is NOT persisted to ticket state, so the assemble step cannot see it unless the flag is also threaded to that step's ctx.inputs. The assemble step is an unenumerated second consumer of the size signal; if only the precheck sees it, an escalated bug would flip det_blocking on but still route only the necessity probe (never the full rubric), so escalation is half-applied.
findings.location: Scope: '_cli/_llm_commands.py (the --size-lines flag ...) + EVERY intermediate seam the value traverses to reach plan_review_precheck's ctx.inputs'
scenarios: review-plan <bug> --size-lines 160: precheck enables blocking but route_criteria still restricts to BUG_TIER_CRITERIA, so the full rubric never runs and AC1's 'escalates to the full blocking rubric' is not met
findings.suggested_fix: In the gate YAML bind the new size input to BOTH the precheck and assemble step `with:` blocks, and have route_criteria (or plan_review_assemble_criteria) read it from ctx.inputs when deciding whether a bug is escalated, mirroring how it already reads probe_criteria.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add size_lines to plan_review_precheck_input.schema.json AND plan_review_assemble_criteria_input.schema.json (both currently additionalProperties:false), the gate YAML inputs: block, and the _run_plan_review() intermediate hop — enumerate these as edit targets in Scope.
evidence: review_plan() (__init__.py:461) delegates to _run_plan_review() (:476-486), an intermediate hop with a fixed kwarg list (no size param) between the facade and the gate-YAML workflow dispatch
gate YAML plan-review.yaml declares its own inputs: block (ticket_id/probe_criteria/subject_plan/prerequisites) — a new size input must be declared here too
findings.finding: The new size_lines step input is an unenumerated edit against two workflow input schemas that will hard-reject it. plan_review_precheck_input.schema.json and plan_review_assemble_criteria_input.schema.json both declare "additionalProperties": false and permit only ticket_id (plus probe_criteria for assemble). Passing a new size_lines input into either step fails schema validation unless the schema is amended. The plan says 'the executor must thread the new key through each hop' but Scope does not list these schemas (nor the intermediate _run_plan_review() facade hop between review_plan() and workflow dispatch) among the seams the value traverses.
findings.location: Scope: 'the review-workflow assemble/inputs plumbing in llm/plan_review (workflow assembly + precheck input construction), and the precheck's ctx.inputs read'
scenarios: Wiring size_lines into the precheck or assemble step `with:` block triggers a schema-validation failure at workflow-engine step-input validation because additionalProperties is false
findings.suggested_fix: List plan_review_precheck_input.schema.json, plan_review_assemble_criteria_input.schema.json, the plan-review.yaml inputs: declaration, and the _run_plan_review() signature as explicit hops the size value must traverse.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the --size-lines value reaches orchestrator.route_criteria (both the assemble-step caller AND the batch-runner fan-in caller) — e.g. thread it onto PlanContext via assemble_context so route_criteria can lift BUG_TIER_CRITERIA — since route_criteria takes only a PlanContext and the Scope currently threads the flag no further than plan_review_precheck's ctx.inputs.
evidence: Approach: 'the SINGLE routing seam that keys the bug tier (registry.BUG_TIER_CRITERIA restriction at ~:221) and is reached by BOTH the assemble step and the batch-runner's project-criteria fan-in, so escalation lands once and covers both callers'
route_criteria signature: 'def route_criteria(ctx: PlanContext, gate_log: dict[str, str] | None = None)' — no inputs param
production_batch_runner.py:272 'single, agent = route_criteria(ctx)' — fan-in caller supplies only a PlanContext, no CLI flag
PlanContext (det_floor.py:120) fields are ticket-store-derived (ticket_type, state, children, repo_root); no size field, and assemble_context(ticket_id, *, repo_root, cfg) takes no size argument
Scope threads the value only 'to reach plan_review_precheck's ctx.inputs' — a StepContext, not the PlanContext route_criteria consumes
findings.finding: The --size-lines escalation signal cannot reach orchestrator.route_criteria (~:190/:221), the seam the plan designates as the SINGLE routing point that keys the bug tier for BOTH callers. route_criteria takes only a PlanContext (assembled from ticket-store reads via assemble_context); it has no ctx.inputs and no field for a CLI flag. The Scope threads the flag only as far as plan_review_precheck's ctx.inputs (a StepContext), which can toggle det_blocking but cannot lift the BUG_TIER_CRITERIA restriction that route_criteria applies. The batch-runner fan-in caller (production_batch_runner._project_criteria -> route_criteria(ctx)) has no access to the flag at all. Result: a --size-lines>150 bug can get blocking enabled in the precheck yet still be routed to only BUG_TIER_CRITERIA=('necessity',) — the full rubric never runs — and the two callers diverge on the size trigger, the exact split centralization was meant to prevent. (The file_impact trigger is unaffected: it lives on ctx.state, which route_criteria already reads.)
findings.location: Approach B1 ('escalation lands once … covers both callers'); Scope bullet threading --size-lines to plan_review_precheck's ctx.inputs; orchestrator.route_criteria ~:190/:214/:221; det_floor.PlanContext:120
scenarios: review-plan <bug> --size-lines 160: precheck enables blocking but route_criteria still restricts to ('necessity',), so no full-rubric finder runs and blocking is over nothing
A bug that escalates via --size-lines through the batch-runner's project-criteria fan-in never escalates there (no ctx.inputs), diverging from the assemble step
findings.suggested_fix: Add the escalation input to PlanContext (e.g. a size_lines / bug_tier_escalated field) populated in assemble_context from the CLI-threaded value, and read it inside route_criteria's bug_tier gate so the full criteria set routes; keep file_impact as the no-flag trigger already available on ctx.state. Extend the Scope's threading list to include assemble_context / PlanContext, not just plan_review_precheck's ctx.inputs.

findings.finding: The plan changes review_plan()'s signature/threading to carry a new --size-lines value into plan_review_precheck's ctx.inputs, but its Scope patch-site inventory names only _llm_commands.py, the review_plan() facade, and 'ctx.inputs' — omitting the mandatory intermediate seams the value must traverse. The probe_criteria feature (the structural analogue of a per-run workflow input) shows the required site set the plan misses: _run_plan_review (__init__.py:476, its own keyword-only param list — every review_plan call flows through it), produce_plan_review_verdict (gate_dispatch.py:79) which must accept a size param AND inject it into the run_workflow input dict (gate_dispatch.py:165-170, currently {ticket_id, probe_criteria, subject_plan, prerequisites}), the gates/plan-review.yaml input declaration + ${{ inputs.* }} wiring (probe_criteria at :23/:53), and the assemble-criteria input schema (plan_review_assemble_criteria_input.schema.json). plan_review_precheck (workflow_ops.py:77-95) reads nothing from ctx.inputs today, so a new read-site is required there. The inventory reads as endpoint-only (CLI + facade + ctx.inputs) rather than symbol-graph-derived across the call chain.
findings.location: Scope: 'src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py (the --size-lines flag) + the llm.review_plan() facade / review-workflow input threading so the size value reaches plan_review_precheck's ctx.inputs (today the facade passes only ref/source/sign/force)'
findings.suggested_fix: Mirror probe_criteria exactly: add size_lines as a keyword param on _run_plan_review and produce_plan_review_verdict, inject it into the run_workflow input dict at gate_dispatch.py:165-170, declare + wire it in gates/plan-review.yaml (like :23/:53) and the assemble-criteria input schema, and read it via ctx.inputs.get('size_lines') in the workflow_ops bug branch.

findings.finding: The plan introduces a new CLI flag (--size-lines), new bug-review-tier escalation semantics, and a new Gerrit blocking criterion, plus an explicit design decision to NOT config-plumb the 150 threshold — but no ADR/doc/AGENTS.md update is planned to capture these, even though the context notes prior bug fixes of this class shipped ADRs.

findings.checklist_item: State an explicit rollback/disable mechanism (e.g. a documented way to turn the B2 blocking criterion off, or expand-contract via an initial advisory-only rollout) for the newly-blocking Gerrit bug-fix gate.
evidence: 'commit trailer ticket is type=bug AND non-test diff >150 lines AND plan_review_status verdict is in the FLAG bucket -> BLOCKING finding'
The plan supplies INFRA-FAIL-OPEN for tooling gaps but no operator-facing kill-switch / rollback for a misclassifying gate on a previously-unblocked path.
findings.finding: B2 introduces a NEW BLOCKING Gerrit DET criterion on a flow (oversized bug-fix commits) that previously always merged, but the plan states no disable/rollback/back-out path if the gate misfires or the cross-host attestation read is systematically wrong in production.
findings.location: Approach B2 / Acceptance Criteria (Gerrit DET criterion blocks oversized bug fixes)
scenarios: The FLAG-bucket classification proves too aggressive on real diffs and blocks legitimate bug fixes; operators need a way to disable the gate without reverting the whole change.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a back-out note: land B2 as advisory-only first (or behind a gate-level toggle) so it can be neutralized without reverting B1, then flip to blocking once the backtest/live signal confirms low FP.

findings.finding: B2's set (b) 'keyring-verification failure classes from the cross-host read (absent / invalid / off-era / untrusted-signer)' names verdict literals that do not exist in the machinery the plan says it reuses. Grep of the codebase returns 0 hits for `absent`, `off-era`, and `untrusted-signer` as verdicts; only `invalid` is real. The actual cross-host verify vocabulary is: `unknown_principal` (authorship.py:506/515 — empty/failed trust root), `mismatch`/`bad-signature`/`key_not_valid_at_era` (registry/opcert/verify_authorship), and the canonical enum (types.py:261) {unsigned, foreign_key, certified, mismatch, key_not_valid_at_era, invalid, unavailable, unknown_kind, unknown_scheme}. The verify-authorship command classifies into {verified, unsigned, unknown-author, bad-signature, key_not_valid_at_era}.
findings.location: Approach B2, 'Verdict buckets (b) keyring-verification failure classes from the cross-host read (absent / invalid / off-era / untrusted-signer)'; AC 'Verdict predicate' and 'coverage unit test pins ... the keyring failure classes'

findings.finding: B2's source-(b) 'keyring-verification failure classes' are named absent/invalid/off-era/untrusted-signer, but the cross-host verification machinery the plan says it reads (verify_authorship_at_commit -> registry.verify / trusted_env.verify_required_environment) emits registry.Verdict.verdict literals certified/mismatch/unknown_kind/unknown_scheme/unknown_principal/key_not_valid_at_era — not those four names.
findings.location: Approach B2, 'Verdict buckets ... (b) keyring-verification failure classes from the cross-host read (absent / invalid / off-era / untrusted-signer)'; AC lines on the verdict predicate + coverage unit test
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the four descriptive labels with the concrete verify verdict literals the machinery returns, or add an explicit mapping table (plan-label -> {registry.Verdict.verdict values}) and have the coverage test pin equality against the concrete verdict enum so no authenticity verdict (mismatch/unknown_principal) can leak into the INFRA fail-open bucket.

findings.finding: B2's named cross-host verification mechanism cannot verify a plan-review attestation: the plan routes through rebar.attest.authorship.verify_authorship_at_commit, but a plan-review attestation is an OPCERT_KIND ('rebar.opcert.v1') DSSE op-cert signed by the ENVIRONMENT principal, whereas verify_authorship_at_commit verifies AUTHORSHIP_KIND ('rebar.authorship.v1') event-level author_sig envelopes against an author-IDENTITY keyring. The correct cross-host verifier for an environment op-cert is rebar.attest.opcert.verify_opcert with the trusted_env pinned environment keyring.
findings.location: Approach §B2 ('reads the attestation through the same cross-host trust root ... rebar.attest.authorship.verify_authorship_at_commit / keys_valid_at_anchor'); Acceptance Criteria bullet 3
findings.suggested_fix: Verify the plan-review op-cert with opcert.verify_opcert (principal = the cert's env_id, keyring = trusted_env.trusted_env_keyring(env_id), anchored on the SIGNATURE event's storage anchor), then feed the verify-then-extract result into compute_validity(profile=DEFAULT, kind='plan-review') for freshness — preserving the shared keys_valid_at_anchor era rule the plan already cites.

findings.finding: The FLAG-bucket's named 'keyring-verification failure classes' {absent / invalid / off-era / untrusted-signer} do not correspond to any real verdict enum from the op-cert or authorship verifiers, so the coverage unit test's exact-set-equality (ACCEPTED ∪ FLAG ∪ INFRA-NAMED = compute_validity literals ∪ keyring failure classes ∪ {error}) cannot be authored against the actual code.
findings.location: Approach §B2 verdict buckets '(b) keyring-verification failure classes ... (absent / invalid / off-era / untrusted-signer)'; Acceptance Criteria bullets 3-4

findings.finding: B2 asserts it can verify a plan-review attestation cross-host by composing `verify_authorship_at_commit`/`keys_valid_at_anchor` with 'trust roots from attest/trusted_env.py', but these are three distinct, non-composed trust roots: verify_authorship verifies rebar.authorship.v1 SSHSIG event signatures against an AUTHOR IDENTITY's keys, while trusted_env.py pins ENVIRONMENT keyrings consumed only by verify-opcert (completion-verifier op-certs). authorship.py imports no trusted_env and knows nothing of plan-review.
findings.location: Approach B2 — 'era-valid keyring verification via attest.authorship + trusted_env trust roots'; Acceptance Criterion 3
findings.suggested_fix: Pick the authorship path (verify_authorship_at_commit against the author identity keyring) and drop the trusted_env reference, OR pick the op-cert/trusted_env path (verify_required_environment) and drop the authorship reference; then confirm that path actually applies to plan-review-kind attestations.

findings.finding: verify_authorship_at_commit consumes a DSSE `Envelope` extracted from a mutating event's `author_sig` (kind rebar.authorship.v1), but plan-review attestations are HMAC records verified by signing.verify_signature and carry no author_sig/DSSE envelope. The plan does not specify how a plan-review manifest becomes an authorship envelope the verifier can accept.
findings.location: Approach B2 — 'reads the attestation through the same cross-host trust root the CI merge-gate already uses (verify_authorship_at_commit / keys_valid_at_anchor)'

findings.finding: The coverage AC pins the keyring-verification failure classes as the exact literal set {absent, invalid, off-era, untrusted-signer}, but the named verifier does not emit those strings — verify_authorship_at_commit/verify_authorship return Verdict verdicts drawn from {verified, unsigned, unknown-author, bad-signature, key_not_valid_at_era, unknown_principal}.
findings.location: Approach B2 bucket (b) and Acceptance Criterion 4 (coverage set equality)

findings.finding: B2's group (b) 'keyring-verification failure classes {absent / invalid / off-era / untrusted-signer}' are not the actual verdict-string vocabulary emitted by the cross-host machinery the plan cites; the executor cannot map the FLAG-bucket rule or the coverage-test enum onto real verdicts.
findings.location: Approach B2, 'Verdict buckets ... (b) keyring-verification failure classes from the cross-host read (absent / invalid / off-era / untrusted-signer)'; and the 4th Acceptance Criterion (coverage unit test pins ACCEPTED u FLAG u INFRA-NAMED = ... u the keyring failure classes u {error})
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate the real verdicts from verify_authorship_at_commit/registry.verify: FLAG = {mismatch, unknown_principal, key_not_valid_at_era, bad-signature} (deterministic un-trustworthy attestation properties); INFRA-FAIL-OPEN = {unknown_kind, unknown_scheme} plus any unlisted future verdict and {error}. Restate group (b) as this literal set and pin the coverage unit test to ACCEPTED u FLAG u INFRA-NAMED = compute_validity's plan-review literals u {the registry.Verdict literals reachable from the cross-host read} u {error}.

findings.finding: The plan names compute_validity as `attest.compute_validity` in `attest.py` under the rebar.attest package, but it actually lives in rebar.llm.plan_review.attest (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:513); rebar.attest contains no compute_validity.
findings.location: Approach B2 — 'attest.compute_validity (profile=DEFAULT, kind=plan-review)' and Scope 'read-only consumers of ... attest.compute_validity'
findings.suggested_fix: Reference rebar.llm.plan_review.attest.compute_validity(..., kind=<the plan-review manifest-prefix constant>, profile=PlanValidityProfile.DEFAULT).
